newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING sees Canadian licence within days.
newsitem.headline: ING sees Canadian licence within days.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV hopes to receive a federal licence in the next few days to start a trust company for direct marketing of services in Canada, executive board chairman Aad Jacobs said.
He told a business luncheon this would be a pilot project for similar initiatives by the Dutch group in the United States and other countries with mature financial services markets.

"This new company, ING Direct, will offer a limited range of savings and loans products through direct marketing, starting next year," Jacobs told the annual luncheon of the Netherlands Canadian Chamber of Commerce.
ING would have to complete extensive application procedures in each Canadian province after winning federal approval.
He said ING had earmarked an initial investment of $50 million to start ING Direct, which would begin in Toronto with about 100 employees.
Unlike Canadian banks which use direct response distribution to support branch networks, ING Direct would derive its business solely from mass media advertising and direct mail.
"ING Direct will concentrate purely on telephone banking, which will enable us to operate in a more cost effective way," Jacobs said.
The main target group would be people in Ontario province aged between 30 and 55 and with an annual income of more than $50,000, but within a year the focus would turn national.
Jacobs said as the ING name was unknown in Canada, the emphasis on advertising would be to build credibility.
ING has operated insurance businesses for 40 years in Canada, where it has 2,900 staff, under other names.
He said the progress of ING Direct would be important for the development of its activities in Canada.
ING would investigate making banking products available through insurance brokers with which it co-operates.
"ING Direct is also a pilot project for similar initiatives in the United States and other countries with mature financial services markets," Jacobs said.
ING Direct is being established in response to a study in 1994 which explored opportunities for direct marketing, a trend which was gaining ground in Anglo-Saxon countries at the time.

The intention was to start a direct response project in a country in which it had been active for a long time, and Canada was chosen over Australia because ING had direct marketing experience through its Belair insurance unit in Canada.
